title: Double-Coupling Hierarchy (Rigid Visitor Pattern)
pattern: Using the object-oriented Visitor Pattern where the `Visitor` interface lists every concrete `Element` subclass, and every subclass implements `accept`.
why_bad: It creates a double-coupling hierarchy. Adding a new `Element` (e.g., `Triangle`) requires modifying and recompiling the entire `Visitor` interface and all of its concrete implementations (e.g., `DrawVisitor`, `ExportVisitor`).
detection: An interface containing specific methods for every concrete implementation in an associated trait hierarchy.
counterexample: Highly static object graphs where elements never change, though enums are still safer in compiled languages.
source: Erich Gamma et al., *Design Patterns* (1994), Chapter 5 ("Visitor").
